question: A concave lens has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the lens. What is the magnification produced by the lens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**+0.33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnification produced by a lens is given by the formula: **m = v / u**, where **v** is the image distance and **u** is the object distance.
 
• For a concave lens, the focal length (**f**) is negative, so here **f = -15 cm**.
 
• The object distance (**u**) is **-30 cm** (negative because the object is placed on the left side of the lens).
 
• Using the lens formula: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, substitute the values: **1/(-15) = 1/v - 1/(-30)**.
 
• After solving, the image distance (**v**) is calculated as **-10 cm**.
 
• Now, calculate magnification: **m = v/u = -10/-30 = +0.33**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Lens:**

 
 
• A concave lens is a diverging lens, meaning it spreads out light rays that are initially parallel.
 
• It always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image irrespective of the object distance.
 
• The focal length of a concave lens is always negative, as it diverges light.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• The lens formula is **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where:
 
 
• **f** = focal length
 
• **v** = image distance
 
• **u** = object distance
 
 
 
• For concave lenses, all distances are taken with proper sign conventions, where:
 
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• The magnification of a lens is given by **m = v/u**.
 
• If magnification (**m**) is negative, the image is inverted. If positive, the image is erect.
 
• For concave lenses, magnification is always less than 1 and positive or negative depending on the nature of the image.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Lenses:**
 
 
• Used in eyeglasses for people with myopia (near-sightedness).
 
• Used in optical instruments like cameras and telescopes to widen the field of view.
 
• Used in flashlight systems to diverge light over a larger area.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Conventions:** In optics, the following sign conventions are used:

 
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
 
• Heights measured upward and perpendicular to the principal axis are positive.
 
• Heights measured downward and perpendicular to the principal axis are negative.
 
 
 
• **Key Numerical Values:**
 
 
• Focal length of the concave lens: **-15 cm**.
 
• Object distance: **-30 cm**.
 
• Calculated image distance: **-10 cm**.
 
• Magnification: **+0.33**.
 
 
 
• **Correct Option:** The correct option is **+0.33**, as calculated using the lens formula and magnification formula.
